cells.tense: What you built holds, and your hands are level on it
cells.act: carry your own share, all of it
cells.ask: Name the recurring piece you carry for a group and hold your whole part of it this week — no passing any of it off, no asking anyone to check on you.
cells.core:
The work is done and it holds. You can point to the thing you carried through to its end. That steadiness is real and it's yours, and none of it needs proving now.

What it can slide into: holding so hard that containment turns into a lid nobody can lift. Name the recurring piece you carry for a group — an arrangement, a standing task, a long-standing habit of the group — and hold your whole share of it this week without handing any of it off and without asking anyone to check on you. You'll feel which parts of the weight are actually yours, and which you picked up by reflex. Setting one down after that reads as a decision, not a collapse.
cells.sheetLine: A made thing holds. You can set it down and pick it up.
cells.verb: Bring a made thing through to a finish

cells.tense: You're ending shared things before they've had a season
cells.act: sit somewhere new with nothing in your hands and let whatever comes, come
cells.ask: Take a shared thing you're about to close, sit with it an hour with your hands empty and no exit plan, and take it in as it is.
cells.core:
Endings arrive in your shared life ahead of schedule. From where you stand, the thing is already stale and closing it feels like air. From inside the shared thing, it comes across as nothing being allowed to stay long enough to matter.

What's thin isn't restraint — it's receiving. The endings come pre-decided because nothing has managed to reach you before you ruled on it. Take a shared thing you're about to close — an arrangement, a practice, a way the group meets — and sit inside it for an hour with your hands empty: no plan, no verdict, no quiet draft of the goodbye. Let the thing itself tell you what it is. Whatever's real in it will still be there after. You'll be choosing then, not bracing.
cells.sheetLine: Endings landing early read as nothing being allowed to stay.
cells.verb: Bring a made thing through to a finish

cells.tense: A build finished and you're staring at the doorway it left
cells.act: describe what is in front of your eyes in five plain lines, no conclusions
cells.ask: Write five plain lines about what's actually there where the finished thing used to sit — the hours, the open slot — with no story about what it means.
cells.core:
Something you carried through to its end is over. Your eyes keep returning to the closed door rather than the cleared ground. The old slot still sits in your week, and hours that something living could use are going into a room that's already finished.

Write five plain lines about what's actually there now — the open hours, the empty slot, the light at that time of day, whatever is honestly within view. No verdict and no story about what it says that the thing ended. Looking comes first. What fills the slot can wait until you've looked, and it doesn't need a meaning to be worth doing.
cells.sheetLine: It ended. The hours are open and nothing is filling them.

cells.tense: You're clearing ground gently and calling it letting things be
cells.ask: Pick a practice or arrangement you've quietly let thin, and look at it two minutes before saying anything about it — to anyone, or to yourself.
cells.core:
Things end around you quietly, and you'd say you're only letting them be. A practice thins because you stopped renewing it. An arrangement goes silent because you stopped turning up. You'd tell it plainly and move on, and the telling is what keeps the ending outside your hands.

Before any decision: look. Pick a practice or arrangement you've been letting thin, and look at it for two minutes without naming what's there — no verdict, no explanation, no quiet case for why it's fine. Looking is what comes before choosing. Nobody has to hear about it. You'll find out whether you meant to let it go, and either answer is yours to keep.
cells.sheetLine: The hand that's clearing is yours, unsigned.

Cut it in the cells and let the act stand on its own.
